_doc: Virgil's lessons (scripts/tutorial/lessons.gd). Each lesson is a guided 1v1 match against the AI.
player / enemy: hero, cards (dealt in this order when 'stacked'; or 'deck': 'starter' = the hero's class starter, shuffled),
opening (opening hand size), health (hero Health), wounds (damage already taken), mana (empty crystals at the start),
board (minions already in play). enemy.hero 'random' = a random hero of another class.
player.choose: true = the player picks their hero (one per class) before the match; 'hero' is then the default.
script: the enemy's turns, in order, as lists of intents: {play: id, target?}, {attack: id|'all', target: 'hero'|id},
{power: true, target?}. A target names a minion by card id (the enemy's own side last) or 'hero'.
After the script: 'after' = 'easy' (the Easy AI) or 'pass'. 'ai': 'easy' plays the whole match with the Easy AI.
steps: Virgil's lines, in order. 'say' text, 'point' / 'mark' (hand:<id>, mine:<id>, foe:<id>, my_hero, foe_hero,
power, end, mana), and how the step ends: 'wait': 'tap' (tap to continue, the board waits), 'do': an action the player
must take (act: play|attack|power|end|inspect, card, target), 'until': 'end_turn'|'win'|'act'|'mulligan' (free play).
'when': 'mulligan' shows the step during the opening-hand choice. In 'say', {tap} / {Tap} reads tap or click by device.

lessons.title: The Ferryman
lessons.learn: Mana, playing minions, attacking and ending your turn.
lessons.outro: The ferryman yields, and the boat is ours. On to the next crossing.

steps.say: Welcome, pilgrim. I am Virgil, and I will be your guide. That is Charon, the ferryman. Bring his Health, the number on the red drop, down to zero and you win.
This is your mana. You gain one more crystal every turn, up to ten, and they all refill when your turn begins.
Every card costs the mana shown in its top corner. Drag the Lost Pilgrim up onto the board to play it.
That is a minion. A new minion is asleep and can only attack from your next turn.
Your mana is spent. Press End Turn and let Charon make his move.
Charon has played a minion of his own. Attack is the number on the left, Health on the right.
Your Pilgrim is awake now. Drag from it to Charon's minion to attack.
In a fight, each minion deals its Attack as damage to the other. Both had 1 Health, so both are gone.
You have 2 mana this turn. Play the Virtuous Pagans.
That is all your mana. End your turn.
Minions can also attack the enemy hero. Nothing stands in the way of Charon himself.
Drag from your Pagans to Charon to strike him.
Now play me: Virgil, the Guide. Read my card. When I arrive, you draw a card.
Well done. End your turn.
Charon's She-wolf bit you, and his hero power struck you as well. Lost Health does not come back on its own.
Charon has 4 Health left. The Pagans and I hit for 2 each. Attack him with both and the crossing is ours.

lessons.title: The Wrathful Knight
lessons.learn: Spells, your hero power, Armor and Guard.
lessons.outro: Filippo sinks back into the mud. The City of Dis lies ahead.

steps.say: Filippo Argenti, the wrathful knight of the Styx, bars the way to the City of Dis. Today you learn spells, your hero power and Guard.
Spells do their work once, then they are gone. Centaur Arrows deals 3 damage to any target you choose.
Drag the Arrows up, then aim at the She-wolf to destroy it.
Three mana spent. End your turn.
See the shield around the Sullen One? That is Guard. While a Guard stands, your attacks must hit it first.
Play the Virtuous Pagans.
Two mana left. Use your hero power, Steadfast, to gain 2 Armor. Every hero has a power: 2 mana, once per turn.
Armor sits on top of your Health and takes damage first. It stays until it is used up.
End your turn.
The Sullen One struck you, but your Armor took the blow.
Filippo hides behind his Guard. Attack the Sullen One with your Pagans.
It still stands. Finish it with Saint Lucy's Light, which deals 2 damage.
The Guard is gone, so every target is open again. Spend the rest of your mana as you like, then end your turn.
Another Guard: Caiaphas. Break through with spells or attacks, then strike Filippo until he falls.

lessons.title: The Two-Horned Flame
lessons.learn: Keywords: Ward, Drain, Venom, Rebirth and Swift. Reading card text.
lessons.outro: Ulysses's flame gutters out. You read every card like an old hand.

steps.say: Ulysses, wrapped in his two-horned flame. A clever foe. This lesson is about keywords: bold words on a card that bend the rules.
Horace has Ward. Rest the pointer on his card, or hold it with your finger, to read what Ward does.
Ward blocks the first damage the minion would take. Play Horace.
You came here wounded. The Hungry Wolf has Drain: the damage it deals also heals your hero. Play it.
End your turn.
Ulysses burned Horace with his hero power, but the Ward took the hit. The Ward is spent; Horace is unhurt.
That serpent has Venom: any minion it damages is destroyed, however big. Trade it for something small.
Send Horace against the serpent.
Both are gone. Venom took Horace, but the serpent will poison nothing else.
Now the Wolf. Attack Ulysses and watch your own Health rise: that is Drain.
The Phoenix has Rebirth: the first time it dies, it comes back with 1 Health. Play it.
The Leopard has Swift: it can attack on the turn it arrives. Play it.
Attack Ulysses with the Leopard at once.
End your turn.
The Phoenix burned and rose again. It keeps its Attack, but it has 1 Health and will not rise a second time.
Read your foe's cards too. On Play happens when a card is played, Last Breath when the minion dies. This Achaean leaves a 2/2 Raider behind.
Ulysses has 6 Health left, and your three minions hit for 3 each. End the voyage.

lessons.title: The Trial
lessons.learn: A real match against an easy opponent, with a few hints along the way.
lessons.outro: You walk the rest of the way on your own now. Hell is wide: go and see it.

steps.say: Now a real match against an easy opponent. First, your opening hand: {tap} any card you want to swap, then press Confirm. Cheap cards help most early on.
From here you play on your own. I will only whisper a hint now and then. Good luck, pilgrim.
